Table 1:Comparison with representative spatial and 3D reasoning benchmarks.✓\checkmarkyes,△\trianglepartial,×\bm{\times}no.3D: volumetric stimuli throughout;Pure: abstract geometric stimuli;Procedural: programmatically generated items;Infinite: generation not limited to a fixed source pool;OE: open-ended answers;Linked: questions on the same item whose answers entail one another, with their agreement evaluated (partial: linked questions without such an analysis);No-image: image-removal controls (partial: image replaced by a text description);Format: matched answer-format comparisons;Probe: visual-feature probes against ground-truth targets.Takeaway:Several benchmarks share individual properties;BedBenchuniquely combines open-ended 3D questions, linked questions checked for agreement, image-removal controls, and probes of frozen visual features, which together locate where a failure arises (Section2).

Each open-weight cell is the 5-run mean for one task×\timesmodel×\timesinference mode condition;the frontier rowsare single-run TH results;the human rowaggregates 30 participants (one question per task per participant; see AppendixC.4).The best-constant rowgives the accuracy of always outputting the most frequent ground-truth answer (or candidate position) for each task.Bold= best model accuracy per task and highest model average. NT = Non-Thinking, TH = Thinking mode.Takeaway:Humans average 70.0%, while the strongest model reaches 51.5%, 14.8 pp above the best-constant average of 36.7%; the gap is largest onT5, where humans reach 93.3% and no model exceeds 7.2%.

Table 80:T2 Packaging, scaling-responsive instance, across the Qwen3.5 (0.8B–35B-A3B) and Gemma4 (E2B–31B, in parentheses) parameter ladders under Non-Thinking mode. Qwen3.5 flips from wrongly answering True at 0.8B–9B to correctly answering False (the object cannot fit the [2,2,2] boundary in any orientation) at 27B/35B-A3B; Gemma4 flips one step earlier, at E4B and up. Both families converge on the correct answer only at their larger checkpoints, mirroring the coarse-cue scaling gains quantified in AppendixB.3.2.

Table 81:T4 Color Count, scaling-responsive instance, across the Qwen3.5 (0.8B–35B-A3B) and Gemma4 (E2B–31B, in parentheses) parameter ladders under Non-Thinking mode. Both families only reach the ground truth (6) at their two largest checkpoints, illustrating the scaling-responsive trend quantified in AppendixB.3.2.

Table 82:T6 Local Structure, scaling-responsive instance, across the Qwen3.5 (0.8B–35B-A3B) and Gemma4 (E2B–31B, in parentheses) parameter ladders under Non-Thinking mode,. The Qwen3.5 ladder flips from wrongly answering True at 0.8B/2B to correctly answering False from 4B upward, the trend quantified in AppendixB.3.2; Gemma4 is already correct at every checkpoint on this instance, so this row demonstrates the Qwen-side scaling gain rather than a matched two-family transition.

Table 83:T7 Color Dominance, scaling-responsive instance, across the Qwen3.5 (0.8B–35B-A3B) and Gemma4 (E2B–31B, in parentheses) parameter ladders under Non-Thinking mode. The two smallest checkpoints in each family over-list several non-dominant colors alongside the correct pair; every checkpoint at 4B/E4B and above converges exactly on the correct two-color set {cyan,yellow}, mirroring the coarse-cue scaling gains quantified in AppendixB.3.2(Figure5).

Table 84:T9 Visible Floors, scaling-responsive instance, across the Qwen3.5 (0.8B–35B-A3B) and Gemma4 (E2B–31B, in parentheses) parameter ladders under Non-Thinking mode. Both families walk from wrongly answering 3 at their two smallest checkpoints to correctly answering 4 (the ground truth) from their third checkpoint upward, the same shape as the T4 instance above; the aggregate T9 curve is noisier in between than T2/T4/T6 (AppendixB.3.2), but this instance isolates the same net small-to-large improvement.

Table 85:T11 Projection, scaling-responsive instance, across the Qwen3.5 (0.8B–35B-A3B) and Gemma4 (E2B–31B, in parentheses) parameter ladders under Non-Thinking mode. Both families flip from the wrong candidate (2) at their two smallest checkpoints to the correct 1 from their third checkpoint upward, the same shape as the T4/T9/T7 instances above, illustrating the responsive trend quantified in AppendixB.3.2(Figure5).

Table 86:T1 Volume, an instance that isolates the family-level asymmetry underlying T1’s aggregate curve in AppendixB.3.2(Figure5): across the Qwen3.5 (0.8B–35B-A3B) and Gemma4 (E2B–31B, in parentheses) parameter ladders under Non-Thinking mode. Qwen3.5 is genuinely scaling-resistant on this instance, landing on the same wrong value (1212) at 5 of its 6 sizes regardless of scale; Gemma4 is scaling-responsive, flipping from wrong (E2B=14=14) to exactly correct (E4B=11=11, 31B=11=11), with a dip back to wrong at the intervening MoE checkpoint (26B-A4B=13=13) consistent with the paper’s broader finding that MoE checkpoints do not reliably help. Aggregated over all 100 rows, Qwen3.5’s 0.8B→\to27B delta on T1 is only+6.4+6.4pp while Gemma4’s E2B→\to31B delta is+26.8+26.8pp, this instance is representative of the two families’ opposite directions.

Table 87:T3 Difference, scaling-resistant instance, across the Qwen3.5 (0.8B–35B-A3B) and Gemma4 (E2B–31B, in parentheses) parameter ladders under Non-Thinking mode. Every one of the 10 sizes misses the (intersection, only-A, only-B) triple, and there is no monotonic approach to GT(2,8,8)(2,8,8)as size grows – e.g. Qwen3.5-27B(10,4,2)(10,4,2)is not closer than Qwen3.5-4B(10,2,2)(10,2,2)– illustrating that scale does not recover the cross-object voxel-set alignment this task requires (AppendixB.3.2).

Table 88:T5 Color Distribution, scaling-resistant instance, across the Qwen3.5 (0.8B–35B-A3B) and Gemma4 (E2B–31B, in parentheses) parameter ladders under Non-Thinking mode. Every model size in both families misassigns the per-color block counts, including the two largest checkpoints per family that solve T4, illustrating that added scale does not recover exact per-color counts (AppendixB.3.2).

Table 89:T8 Silhouette Symmetry, scaling-resistant instance, across the Qwen3.5 (0.8B–35B-A3B) and Gemma4 (E2B–31B, in parentheses) parameter ladders under Non-Thinking mode. All 10 sizes in both families answer False on a silhouette that is in fact symmetric (GT True), never once pairing the mirrored columns needed to detect it; the modal answer does not shift with scale, illustrating a scale-invariant default-to-False response under uncertainty at every point on the ladder (AppendixB.3.2).

Table 90:T10 Color Connected, scaling-resistant instance, across the Qwen3.5 (0.8B–35B-A3B) and Gemma4 (E2B–31B, in parentheses) parameter ladders under Non-Thinking mode. The entire Qwen3.5 ladder answers True (wrong) at every size from 0.8B to 35B-A3B, showing no scaling trend; Gemma4 is correct at E2B/E4B/26B-A4B but regresses back to the wrong answer at its largest checkpoint (31B). Neither family shows the monotonic small-to-large convergence seen for the responsive tasks above, illustrating T10’s flat aggregate curve in AppendixB.3.2(Figure5).

Table 91:T12 Reconstruct, scaling-resistant instance, across the Qwen3.5 (0.8B–35B-A3B) and Gemma4 (E2B–31B, in parentheses) parameter ladders under Non-Thinking mode. All 10 sizes across both families collapse onto the same wrong candidate (1), never selecting the correct 0: added scale changes nothing about which cross-view silhouette is picked.

Table 92:T13 Mixture-of-Shapes, scaling-resistant instance, across the Qwen3.5 (0.8B–35B-A3B) and Gemma4 (E2B–31B, in parentheses) parameter ladders under Non-Thinking mode. All 10 sizes across both families collapse onto the same correct candidate (2). This example shows agreement across scales; it is not an instance of persistent failure. The aggregate scaling trends are reported in AppendixB.3.2.
